stories.title: Revisiting the Superclásico: a story of death, violence, colour and family
summary: Attending Boca v River in the week I turned 60 made me recall a lifetime of experiences at the fixtureEver since the Observer Sport Monthly published a list of 50 sporting things you must do before you die with Watch Boca Juniors Play River Plate in Buenos Aires at No 1 in 2004, the biggest super derby in Argentina has been firmly positioned in the global imagination; its reputation for colour, passion and uncontainable emotion acquiring an almost glamorous sheen.

The thump and thud of the coordinated chants, the shiny ticker-tape amid flare smoke matching the teams’ strips, the bounce of the concrete as tens of thousands jump in unison, mounted police surrounding the stadium, avalanche stoppers set alight, rockets aimed at players; blood and fire.Exciting, right?

stories.title: Stumbling block: Wirtz's and Liverpool’s costly struggles against tight defences | Andrew Beasley
summary: The margins tend to be fine when recording statistical outliers.If Alexis Mac Allister’s floated ball from distance into David Raya’s waiting arms had actually counted as a shot, would Andoni Iraola’s side have delivered a markedly better attacking performance?
Far more concerning for the Spaniard will be that his team had 52 touches in the Arsenal penalty area (which is good) to create only one Opta‑defined big chance (which is bad).
The Premier League average this season is five times more efficient; 10.3 box touches per big chance.
